content.text: Draft will treat proof-of-work as additive: it gates secret-bearing attempts, keeps passwordless/code-less paths and existing throttling/auth behavior intact, and documents undecided security policy separately.

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /home/oem/IdeaProjects/testcenter2/brute.md
+# Brute-force protection acceptance criteria
+
+Status: draft for discussion. Derived from `migrate-pr-proofofwork`.
+
+## Goal
+
+Protect credential-bearing session creation with a transparent ALTCHA proof-of-work challenge. Preserve existing authentication, authorization, navigation, and failed-login behavior after a proof is accepted.
+
+## Configuration
+
+### AC1 — Select protected flows independently
+
+Given `BRUTE_FORCE_PROTECTION` contains a space-separated combination of `admin`, `login`, and `person`, when configuration is loaded, then only the listed flows require proof-of-work.
+
+| Config value | Protected submission | Submission not gated |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `admin` | Admin name and password | Login and person flows |
+| `login` | Login name with a non-empty password | Passwordless Login |
+| `person` | Person code | Person continuation without a code |
+| empty | none | all existing flows |
+
+The frontend receives the effective list from the backend system configuration. Changing the setting requires no frontend rebuild.
+
+### AC2 — Keep the signing key server-side
+
+Given a deployment starts, then `SERVER_KEY` is available to the backend through Docker Compose and Helm configuration and is never exposed through frontend configuration or challenge responses.
+
+## Challenge flow
+
+### AC3 — Issue a challenge before checking credentials
+
+Given a protected submission, when the user submits it, then the frontend first requests a backend-signed SHA-256 challenge containing the submitted flow and credentials or code.
+
+Creating a challenge does not authenticate credentials, create a session, or increment failed-login counters.
+
+### AC4 — Bind proof to the submitted attempt
+
+Given a challenge was issued for one flow and one set of submitted values, when its flow, name, password, or code is changed, then its proof is invalid and cannot authenticate the changed attempt.
+
+Unsupported flow values are rejected without attempting authentication.
+
+### AC5 — Solve transparently in the browser
+
+Given a protected challenge is returned, when the frontend receives it, then it solves the challenge in browser workers and submits the solution without an additional user interaction.
+
+While solving, the relevant submit action shows progress and cannot be submitted again. After any failure, progress ends and submission becomes available again.
+
+### AC6 — Verify before authentication
+
+Given a solution is missing, malformed, incorrectly signed, or incorrect, when it is submitted, then the backend returns a client error and does not check credentials or create a session.
+
+Given a valid solution, when it is submitted, then the backend authenticates only the values bound to that challenge and returns the same authorization data as the existing direct flow.
+
+For a person challenge, the valid Login token used to request the challenge is also required when submitting its solution.
+
+### AC7 — Prevent direct bypass
+
+Given a flow is protected, when a caller sends its secret-bearing submission directly to the legacy session endpoint without a valid proof, then the backend rejects it.
+
+Passwordless Logins and person continuation without a code remain available without proof because they contain no secret to brute-force.
+
+## Compatibility and user experience
+
+### AC8 — Preserve successful outcomes
+
+Given a valid proof and valid credentials or code, when authentication succeeds, then session creation, returned access rights, theme selection, and post-login navigation match the behavior before this feature.
+
+### AC9 — Preserve authentication failures and throttling
+
+Given a valid proof but invalid credentials or code, when authentication fails, then the existing user-facing error and failed-login accounting apply.
+
+The existing Admin delay and the existing failed-login limit remain active. Reaching the existing limit still returns `429`.
+
+### AC10 — Load ALTCHA only when needed
+
+Given a flow is protected, when its login component is rendered, then the ALTCHA library is loaded asynchronously.
+
+Given no rendered login component needs protection, then the library is not loaded and adds no work to initial application loading.
+
+## Deployment
+
+### AC11 — Support current deployment paths
+
+Docker Compose and Helm can configure the protected flow list and server signing key. An empty protected-flow list disables the feature without changing existing session behavior.
+
+## Decisions to confirm
+
+1. Should fresh installations enable all three flows by default, while existing installations without configuration remain unprotected?
+2. Must challenges expire or be single-use, or is a reusable proof bound to one exact attempt acceptable?
+3. Should unknown `BRUTE_FORCE_PROTECTION` values fail startup or be ignored?
+
+## Out of scope
+
+- Changing credential rules or access rights
+- Replacing existing failed-login throttling
+- Adding a visible CAPTCHA
*** End Patch";
text(await tools.apply_patch(patch));
